title: Temple of Vespasian and Titus
visualBrief: Surviving southeast pronaos corner: exactly three fluted pale Corinthian columns with moulded bases, leafy/corner-volute capitals and the broken L-shaped surviving entablature, with low mapped podium/cella wall fragments and an open destroyed temple interior. No intact cella, roof, full pediment, complete peristyle or ancient full-temple reconstruction. Preserve Tabularium and independent neighboring ruins.

sourceFacts.horizontalBasis: Exact-QID relation1767603 gives the archaeological extent/axis, not an intact temple shell. Standard PMTiles corner-footing52776559974420 fixes the southeast surviving group. Internal angle +0.580061860533rad, native east/south at runtime heading0. Twelve mapped internal remnant controls are authored; three Portico-side controls outside the relation are independent. Column centers, heights, low remnant heights and their local podium levels are picture-led approximations.
sourceFacts.architecturalHeights: About15.2m column including base/capital; surviving entablature about17.8m above the corner footing. Relative proportions are picture-led; detailed conservation dimensions are not claimed. The inspected pictures guide deep shaft flutes, layered round bases, two leafy capital rows/corner volutes, concave abaci, the broken L-shaped fascia/cornice and taller rough entablature core. Fine sacrifice reliefs, letters, repair pins and exact ancient carving are simplified.
